sources.fullCitation: Photograph of Ivie Anderson. Photographer unidentified; undated. Slide (photograph), 2 × 2 in. Bette Cox Collection, University of California, Los Angeles, Ethnomusicology Archive, call number calauem_200901_ams0000060. Digitised by California Revealed; copy in the Internet Archive, identifier calauem_006181.
sources.researchNote: The institutional description accompanying the photograph, preserved in the Internet Archive metadata for calauem_006181, also documents Anderson's performance of All God’s Children Got Rhythm in A Day at the Races (MGM, 1937), describing it as a rare performance independently of the Duke Ellington orchestra. This contextual description, rather than the photograph itself, supports the linked performance credit.

media.title: Ivie Anderson — portrait photograph
media.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of the singer Ivie Anderson, smiling, arms folded.
media.publicCaption: Ivie Anderson, vocalist with the Duke Ellington orchestra, who sang “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm” in A Day at the Races (1937). Undated slide inscribed “Ivy Anderson”.
media.publicCreditLine: Bette Cox Collection, University of California, Los Angeles, Ethnomusicology Archive; digitised by California Revealed.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The UCLA Ethnomusicology Archive records the copyright status as unknown, states that the work is accessible for education and research, and reports that it searched for rights owners without success. A reduced-resolution reproduction (1100 × 1197 px) is used here for scholarly identification of the singer who introduced “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm” on screen.
